name: EF Core + PostgreSQL
description: EF Core with the Npgsql provider and dotnet-ef migrations, for ASP.NET Core.

specSections.title: Data Model & Migrations
specSections.guidance: For each entity/table: columns with types, lengths and numeric precision, nullability and defaults; the primary key (UUIDv7 or identity); foreign keys with an explicit on-delete behaviour; unique indexes from business rules (say which are case-insensitive); check constraints; indexes for foreign keys and query predicates; enums stored as strings; UTC timestamps; and which aggregates are edited concurrently and need a concurrency token (409 CONFLICT). Then the migration plan: one migration per change, named, in order, with which steps are expand/contract (add, backfill, switch code, drop later) so the previous version keeps working during rollout; any data backfill; the reference/seed data (dev-only seed per role and state); and how migrations run in each environment (an EF migration bundle run as the platform's pre-deploy step, never at app start).

order.reason: Migrations come before the endpoints that use their tables.

exclusive.reason: The data engineer owns the schema, not endpoints or DTOs; those are backend steps.

protectedPaths.reason: Migrations on the base commit are immutable (FR-125); a schema change is a new migration. Only the EF Core model snapshot is updated.

requiredEnv.description: PostgreSQL connection for the API. A postgres:// URI (Render internalConnectionString, Railway ${{Postgres.DATABASE_URL}}, the Supabase session pooler, or External), converted once to an Npgsql connection string with SSL Mode=Require; the migration bundle resolves it the same way.

checklist.item: Exactly one new migration per schema change, never an edit to a migration that exists on the base commit.
Breaking changes (rename, drop, type change) use expand/contract so the previous version runs against the new schema during preview and production rollout.
Columns are explicit (lengths, precision, nullability), foreign keys have a deliberate on-delete, and every foreign key and query predicate is indexed.
Uniqueness rules from the spec are unique indexes or constraints (case-insensitive where the spec says so), and concurrently edited aggregates have a concurrency token mapped to 409 CONFLICT.
Timestamps are UTC (timestamptz/datetimeoffset) from an injected clock, and enums are stored as strings.
Integration tests run against the real engine in a container with every migration applied; no in-memory or SQLite substitute.
Queries are parameterised, project only the needed columns, paginate lists and avoid N+1.
The seed is idempotent, dev-only and gated; reference data is part of the migrations.
No EnsureCreated(), Database.Migrate() or MigrateAsync() in app code; the migration bundle runs as the one-off pre-start step.
Each migration has its .Designer.cs and the model snapshot is updated to match (CI: dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes).
Entity configuration is explicit (IEntityTypeConfiguration per entity), and DbUpdateConcurrencyException maps to 409 CONFLICT.
PostgreSQL specifics are right: snake_case naming, citext for case-insensitive uniqueness, xmin row version, and UTC-only timestamptz values.
